A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching main experiments and Appendices A-I. Text, tables, figures, and the later version's additional appendix and checklist are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments on dataset repetition, weight decay, document sampling, deduplication, and continual pre-training, including CORE and MMLU results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds FastText-only count-manipulation results in Appendix J, Table 7.

M1.justification: The repetition recipe, weight-decay adaptation, greedy and linear count manipulation, and worst-rank ensemble remain unchanged. Appendix J explains existing procedures; its FastText-only comparisons use a scoring approach already present in v1's constrained-data experiments.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same DCLM-baseline, RefinedWeb, and C4 coverage and retain the downstream evaluations. Appendix J compares scoring variants within the existing DCLM experiment rather than adding a dataset, domain, task, or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds FastText-only Greedy 4 copies, Greedy 1 copy, and Linear up to 4 copies to the comparison previously reported in Table 3. FastText was already used in the separate constrained-data Table 4, but these comparators were absent from the corresponding full-pool comparison.

E3.justification: The added scoring comparisons extend Table 3's 7B-model, 138B-token setting and CORE/MMLU evaluation. No retained training budget, model size, evaluation metric, split, or testing procedure is revised. Hardware and sampling details newly supplied elsewhere are disclosures about the existing setup.

E4.justification: Appendix J.3 adds an ablation comparing FastText alone against the FastText/duplication-count ensemble under the same sampling strategies. This tests the contribution of the ranking signal. Existing repetition, weight-decay, curriculum, and deduplication analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The new checklist explicitly states that error bars are not reported because repeated large training runs are impractical; v1 provides no such explanation. This adds information about replication and uncertainty reporting, without supplying exact run counts, seeds, intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 7 adds FastText-only CORE/MMLU scores of 41.6/45.3 for Greedy 4 copies, 45.5/45.4 for Greedy 1 copy, and 42.1/46.7 for Linear up to 4 copies. The linear ensemble retains 46.0/44.2, revealing a CORE/MMLU tradeoff. Previously reported tables and figure results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix J.1 adds the explicit allocation formula bucket_size = goal_docs / sum_{i=1}^{max_copies} i for the linear strategy. v1 supplies a qualitative linear-function description and generic pseudocode. This is a limited added mathematical specification of the retained procedure, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged in wording, and the introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: appropriately regularized repetition can preserve filtered-data advantages, and document-level count manipulation can improve datasets under token constraints.

C2.justification: Appendix J.2 explicitly qualifies ensemble metrics as needing to be fine-grained as well as correlated with quality. Section 2 adds modality and filtering differences as explanations for disagreement with the cited CLIP findings. Existing domain, scale, and bias limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix J expands the sampling description with threshold selection, copy-count buckets, and explicit ensemble-rank calculation. Appendix A newly identifies H100 and TPU hardware and asset licenses. The checklist adds code/data availability statements and acknowledges missing runtime and total-cost information; these are disclosures rather than demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: The cited-work set is retained, but the discussion of Goyal et al. revises the quoted dataset sizes from 12.8B/128B to 12.8M/128M and explicitly distinguishes its modality and filtering techniques. The repeatability discussion also clarifies the relationship to Muennighoff et al.; overall positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording and grammar edits, adds section signposting and a clearer repeatability explanation, and revises affiliations and citation style. Appendix J and a conference checklist are appended, while the main narrative and existing section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a two-column format to a single-column NeurIPS layout, substantially changing figure sizes, table and listing placement, headers, and text flow. Captions for Figures 1, 2, and 5 expand, and Table 7 is added. Existing graphical results are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix J makes the sampling procedure more reproducible and adds a useful scoring ablation that exposes differing CORE and MMLU outcomes. Hardware and licensing disclosures and clearer explanations improve transparency. These are limited gains: the central evidence and claims remain unchanged, and the newly acknowledged lack of statistical uncertainty reporting is not resolved.
